¿Por qué Países Bajos es un destino popu: Why is the Netherlands a popular destination for studying a degree?
Países Bajos combina una educación de al: The Netherlands combines internationally recognised high-quality education, a large number of English-taught degrees, a very high level of English among the local population, proximity to Spain (2–3 hour flights), and a safe, highly international environment in its main university cities.

Países Bajos es el país de la Europa con: The Netherlands has the largest range of English-taught university programmes in continental Europe, with hundreds of degrees and master's programmes taught entirely in English at both research universities and universities of applied sciences.

Entre las más populares para estudiantes: Popular cities for international students include Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht, The Hague, Delft, Groningen, Maastricht, Eindhoven, Leiden and Tilburg, each with its own character, academic offering and living costs.
¿Es muy distinto el sistema educativo ne: Is the Dutch education system very different from Spain's?
Sí. El sistema neerlandés suele ser más: Yes. The Dutch system tends to be more practical, participatory and based on group work and projects, with fewer lectures than in Spain and a closer, less hierarchical relationship between teachers and students.

Las \"research universities\" (universit: Research universities (universiteiten, WO) take a more theoretical, academic and research-oriented approach. Universities of applied sciences (hogescholen, HBO) are more practical, with more work placements and a direct focus on the job market. Both routes are valid and recognised; the choice depends on the student's profile and interests.
¿Cuánto dura un grado universitario (bac: How long does a bachelor's degree in the Netherlands take?
La mayoría de los bachelors en universid: Most bachelor's degrees at research universities (WO) take 3 years, while those at universities of applied sciences (HBO) usually take 4 years, as they include more work placements.
¿Cómo se organiza el curso académico en: How is the academic year organised in the Netherlands?
El curso empieza normalmente en septiemb: The academic year usually starts in September, although some programmes also have a February intake. It is divided into two semesters, each organised into shorter blocks or periods, with exams at the end of each block rather than all at the end of the semester.
¿Cómo funciona el sistema de calificacio: How does the Dutch grading system work?
Se usa una escala del 1 al 10, donde un: It uses a scale from 1 to 10. A 10 is almost unattainable, an 8 is already considered a very high grade, and a 6 is a solid pass. It differs from the Spanish system, and many international students need time to adjust.
Es un sistema propio de las universidade: This is a Dutch university system requiring students to pass a minimum number of credits (ECTS) by the end of the first year to continue the programme at that university. Son la unidad de medida del volumen de t: They measure academic workload and are used throughout the European Higher Education Area. A full year of a Dutch bachelor's degree usually equals 60 ECTS.
¿Se pueden convalidar los estudios cursa: Can studies completed in the Netherlands be recognised if I return to Spain?
En general sí, gracias al sistema europe: Generally yes, thanks to the European ECTS credit system, although each subject or degree recognition request is assessed individually by the receiving university in Spain.
¿Existen dobles grados o programas conju: Are there double degrees or joint programmes with other European universities?
Sí, cada vez es más habitual encontrar p: Yes. Joint programmes between Dutch and other European universities are becoming more common, especially at master's level, although some bachelor's options also exist.
Es un sistema de plazas limitadas que ap: It is a limited-place system used by some high-demand degrees, such as Medicine, Psychology and Physiotherapy, at certain universities. Admission requires more than meeting minimum requirements: there is an additional selection process, such as a test, grade ranking or interview.
¿Qué requisitos académicos piden las uni: What academic requirements do Dutch universities set for Spanish students?
Generalmente se exige haber completado e: They generally require completion of Spanish Bachillerato and a university entrance grade, as well as programme-specific requirements such as subjects studied, minimum grades and language proficiency.

La mayoría de programas piden un nivel e: Most programmes require the equivalent of B2 or C1, demonstrated through official exams such as IELTS or TOEFL. Some universities accept other evidence, such as completing Bachillerato in a bilingual programme.

No siempre. Algunas universidades acepta: Not always. Some universities accept alternative certificates or exemptions if the student completed part of their previous education in English, but each university sets its own criteria.
Studielink es el portal oficial del gobi: Studielink is the Dutch government's official portal for enrolment at any university in the Netherlands. It is a mandatory step for all students wishing to study a bachelor's or master's in the country, regardless of nationality.
¿Cuándo empieza y termina el plazo de ad: When do applications open and close for a September start?
Los plazos varían según la universidad y: Deadlines vary by university and programme. Applications generally open in October or November of the previous year, and the main deadline is usually 1 May, or earlier for numerus fixus programmes. Check the exact dates for each programme every year.
¿Necesito escribir una carta de motivaci: Do I need to write a motivation letter or attend an interview?
Depende del programa. Muchos grados con: It depends on the programme. Many high-demand or numerus fixus degrees require a motivation letter, CV and sometimes an interview or additional selection test. Other programmes admit students who meet the academic and language requirements.
¿Cuánto tiempo antes debería empezar a p: How far in advance should I prepare my application?
Se recomienda empezar entre 6 y 12 meses: Starting 6–12 months before the academic year is recommended. There are strict administrative deadlines for registration, language exams and documents, while finding accommodation also requires considerable advance planning.
Si repito curso o tengo asignaturas pend: Can I still apply if I repeat a year or have outstanding Bachillerato subjects?
En muchos casos sí es posible, aunque pu: In many cases yes, although this may affect deadlines and the documents required at each stage of admission.
¿Cuánto cuesta la matrícula universitari: How much are university tuition fees in the Netherlands for an EU student?
Los estudiantes de la Unión Europea paga: EU students pay the statutory fee, usually around €2,700 per year. The Dutch government sets the exact amount each academic year, and it may vary slightly.
¿Las tasas son más altas para estudiante: Are fees higher for non-EU students?
Sí, los estudiantes de fuera de la Unión: Yes. Non-EU students pay the institutional fee, which is considerably higher and varies widely by university and programme, from several thousand euros to more than €15,000 per year.
¿Hay diferencia de precio entre universi: Is there a price difference between universities of applied sciences and research universities?
La tasa estatutaria para estudiantes de: The statutory fee for EU students is usually similar at both types of institution, although there may be small differences between individual universities.
¿Cuál es el coste de vida aproximado de: What is the approximate cost of living for a student in the Netherlands?
Varía mucho según la ciudad (Ámsterdam e: It varies considerably by city: Amsterdam is notably more expensive than Groningen or Tilburg. Accommodation, mandatory health insurance, food, transport and leisure are the main monthly expenses. The total is usually around €1,500–€1,700 per month.
¿Cuál es la ciudad más cara para vivir c: Which Dutch city is the most expensive for students?
Ámsterdam es, con diferencia, la ciudad: Amsterdam is by far the most expensive, especially for accommodation. Rotterdam, Utrecht, Groningen, Tilburg and Maastricht generally offer a more affordable cost of living.
DUO (Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs) es el: DUO (Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs) is the Dutch public body responsible for student finance in the Netherlands, including loans for tuition fees, living costs and transport.

En ese caso, normalmente sí es necesario: You will usually need a residence permit and, depending on your country of origin, an entry visa (MVV). The university normally manages or helps with this process together with the student.
¿Qué es el BSN y por qué es tan importan: What is a BSN and why is it so important?
El BSN (Burgerservicenummer) es el númer: The BSN (Burgerservicenummer) is your Dutch personal identification number for administrative matters, similar to a DNI/NIE.
